title: Differentially Private One Permutation Hashing

contributions.purpose: Provide differential-privacy (DP) protection for the output sketches of one permutation hashing (OPH), the state-of-the-art efficient method for approximating binary Jaccard similarity, which had not been well studied under DP.
contributions.mechanism: Propose the DP-OPH framework with three variants (DP-OPH-fix, DP-OPH-re, DP-OPH-rand) corresponding to fixed densification, re-randomized densification, and no densification for handling empty OPH bins, in the practical setup where algorithm randomness is external/public; provide algorithm design plus privacy and utility analysis for each.
contributions.evaluation: Theoretical privacy and utility analysis for each of the three variants; attribute-level DP guarantee (neighboring vectors differ in one dimension) proven.
contributions.source_quote: We develop three variants under the DP-OPH framework, DP-OPH-fix, DP-OPH-re, and DP-OPH-rand, corresponding to fixed densification, re-randomized densification, and no densification for OPH, respectively. We provide detailed algorithm design and privacy analysis for each variant, and compare them with a DP MinHash (DP-MH) method.

contributions.purpose: Establish that DP-OPH outperforms the existing DP MinHash baseline and characterize which variant to use in which privacy regime.
contributions.mechanism: Retrieval/similarity-search experiments comparing DP-OPH variants against DP-MH across privacy levels, plus analysis of densification strategy trade-offs.
contributions.evaluation: DP-OPH substantially improves over DP-MH on retrieval; re-randomized densification superior to fixed; DP-OPH-rand best when privacy budget epsilon is small, DP-OPH-re best when epsilon is larger.
contributions.source_quote: In our retrieval experiments, we show that the proposed DP-OPH method substantially improves DP-MH, and re-randomized densification is superior over fixed densification in terms of differential privacy. DP-OPH-rand performs the best when E is small, while DP-OPH-re is the most performant in when larger E is allowed.

contributions.purpose: Extend the DP hashing approach beyond binary data to real-valued / non-negative data for the weighted Jaccard similarity.
contributions.mechanism: Develop DP-BCWS, built on bin-wise consistent weighted samples (BCWS), as a DP algorithm for weighted Jaccard similarity on non-negative data (presented in the appendix).
contributions.evaluation: Qualitative: presented as an extension in Appendix A with algorithm design; no headline metric in main text.
contributions.source_quote: We also extend our algorithms to real-value datasets and develop DP-BCWS algorithm in Appendix A.

self_declared_provenance.quote: In Appendix A, we also provide DP-BCWS which is based on bin-wise consistent weighted samples (BCWS) (Li et al., 2019) for weighted Jaccard similarity (for non-negative data).

In a related work, Aumuller et al. (2020) also proposed to apply randomized response to MinHash. However, the authors incorrectly used a tail bound for the binomial distribution ... their method does not satisfy DP. In our Algorithm 6, we fix it by using the exact probability mass function to compute the tail probability.

notes: Results are net-positive vs the DP-MH baseline. Trade-off/nuance flagged by authors: no single variant dominates - DP-OPH-rand wins at small epsilon, DP-OPH-re wins at larger epsilon (variant choice is regime-dependent). Also corrects a flaw in prior work (Aumuller et al. 2020) whose method did not actually satisfy DP. Paper was rejected. No negative result against own method.
